chapter.li: LEChapter27 Verse1 And when it was determined that we should sail into Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners unto one named Julius, a centurion of Augustus’ band. VerseEnd Verse2 And entering into a ship of Adramyttium, we launched, meaning to sail by the coasts of Asia — one Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us. VerseEnd Verse3 And the next day, we touched at Sidon. And Julius courteously treated Paul, and gave him liberty to go unto his friends to refresh himself. VerseEnd Verse4 And when we had launched from there, we sailed under Cyprus because the winds were contrary. VerseEnd Verse5 And when we had sailed over the sea of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, a city of Lycia. VerseEnd Verse6 And there the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing into Italy, and he put us therein. VerseEnd Verse7 And when we had sailed slowly many days, and scarcely had arrived off Cnidus, the wind not suffering us, we sailed under Crete, off Salmone, VerseEnd Verse8 and, passing it with difficulty, came unto a place which is called the Fair Havens, near unto which was the city of Lasea. VerseEnd

Verse9 Now when much time was spent, and when sailing was now dangerous because the fast was now already past, Paul admonished them VerseEnd Verse10 and said unto them, Sirs, I perceive that this voyage will be with hurt and much damage — not only of the load and ship, but also of our lives. VerseEnd Verse11 Nevertheless, the centurion believed the master and the owner of the ship more than those things which were spoken by Paul. VerseEnd Verse12 And because the haven was not suitable to winter in, the more part advised to depart from there also, if by any means they might attain to Phoenix and there to winter, which is a haven of Crete and lies toward the southwest and northwest. VerseEnd Verse13 And when the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, weighing anchor from there, they sailed close by Crete. VerseEnd

Verse14 But not long after, there arose against it a tempestuous wind called Euroclydon. VerseEnd Verse15 And when the ship was caught and could not bear up into the wind, we let her drive. VerseEnd Verse16 And running under a certain island which is called Clauda, it took much work to gain control of the boat, VerseEnd Verse17 which when they had taken up, they used supporting ropes undergirding the ship, and (fearing lest they should fall into the quicksands) struck sail, and so were driven. VerseEnd Verse18 And we being exceedingly tossed with a tempest, the next day they lightened the ship. VerseEnd Verse19 And the third day, we cast out with our own hands the tackling of the ship. VerseEnd Verse20 And when neither sun nor stars in many days appeared, and no small tempest lay on us, all hope that we should be saved was then taken away. VerseEnd

Verse21 But after long abstinence, Paul stood forth in the midst of them and said, Sirs, you should have listened unto me, and not have set sail from Crete, and to have incurred this harm and loss. VerseEnd Verse22 And now I exhort you to be of good cheer, for there shall be no loss of any man’s life among you, but of the ship. VerseEnd Verse23 For there stood by me this night the angel of God, whose I am and whom I serve, VerseEnd Verse24 saying, Fear not, Paul. You must be brought before Caesar, and behold, God has given you all them that sail with you. VerseEnd Verse25 Wherefore, sirs, be of good cheer, for I believe God, that it shall be even as it was told me. VerseEnd Verse26 Nevertheless, we must be cast upon a certain island. VerseEnd

Verse27 But when the fourteenth night had come, as we were driven up and down in Adria, about midnight, the shipmen deemed that they drew near to some country, VerseEnd Verse28 and sounded and found it twenty fathoms. And when they had gone a little further, they sounded again and found it fifteen fathoms. VerseEnd Verse29 Then, fearing lest we should have fallen upon rocks, they cast four anchors out of the stern and wished for the day. VerseEnd Verse30 And as the shipmen were about to flee out of the ship, when they had let down the boat into the sea under pretext as though they would have cast anchors out of the bow, VerseEnd Verse31 Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, Except these abide in the ship, you cannot be saved. VerseEnd Verse32 Then the soldiers cut off the ropes of the boat and let her fall off. VerseEnd

Verse33 And while the day was coming on, Paul implored them all to take food, saying, This day is the fourteenth day that you have remained and continued fasting, having taken nothing. VerseEnd Verse34 Wherefore, I urge you to take some food, for this is for your health, for there shall not a hair fall from the head of any of you. VerseEnd Verse35 And when he had thus spoken, he took bread and gave thanks to God in presence of them all; and when he had broken it, he began to eat. VerseEnd Verse36 Then were they all of good cheer, and they also took some food. VerseEnd Verse37 And we were in all in the ship two hundred seventy-six souls. VerseEnd Verse38 And when they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship and cast out the wheat into the sea. VerseEnd

Verse39 And when it was day, they knew not the land, but they discovered a certain creek with a shore, into which they determined, if it were possible, to thrust in the ship. VerseEnd Verse40 And when they had taken up the anchors, they committed themselves unto the sea, and loosened the rudder bands, and hoisted up the mainsail to the wind, and made toward shore. VerseEnd Verse41 And falling into a place where two seas met, they ran the ship aground. And the bow stuck fast and remained immovable, but the stern was broken with the violence of the waves. VerseEnd Verse42 And the soldiers’ counsel was to kill the prisoners, lest any of them should swim out and escape. VerseEnd Verse43 But the centurion, desiring to save Paul, kept them from their purpose, and commanded that they who could swim should cast themselves first into the sea and get to land, VerseEnd Verse44 and the rest, some on boards and some on broken pieces of the ship. And so it came to pass that they escaped all safe to land. VerseEnd

LEChapter28 Verse1 And when they had escaped, then they knew that the island was called Malta. VerseEnd Verse2 And the foreign people showed us no little kindness, for they kindled a fire and received us every one because of the present rain and because of the cold. VerseEnd Verse3 And when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks and laid them on the fire, there came a viper out of the heat and fastened on his hand. VerseEnd Verse4 And when the foreigners saw the venomous beast hang on his hand, they said among themselves, No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he has escaped the sea, yet vengeance suffers not to live. VerseEnd Verse5 And he shook off the beast into the fire and felt no harm. VerseEnd Verse6 Nevertheless, they watched when he should have swollen or fallen down dead suddenly; but after they had watched a great while and saw no harm come to him, they changed their minds and said that he was a god. VerseEnd

Verse7 In the same quarters were possessions of the chief man of the island, whose name was Publius, who received us and lodged us three days courteously. VerseEnd Verse8 And it came to pass that the father of Publius lay sick of a fever and dysentery, to whom Paul entered in and prayed, and laid his hands on him and healed him. VerseEnd Verse9 So when this was done, others also who had diseases in the island came and were healed, VerseEnd Verse10 who also honored us with many honors; and when we departed, they loaded us with such things as were necessary. VerseEnd

Verse11 And after three months, we departed in a ship of Alexandria which had wintered in the isle, whose sign was Castor and Pollux. VerseEnd Verse12 And landing at Syracuse, we remained there three days, VerseEnd Verse13 and from there we turned about and came to Rhegium. And after one day, the south wind blew, and we came the next day to Puteoli, VerseEnd Verse14 where we found brethren and were desired to remain with them seven days; and so we went toward Rome. VerseEnd Verse15 And from there, when the brethren heard of us, they came to meet us as far as Appii forum and the Three Taverns, whom when Paul saw, he thanked God and took courage. VerseEnd Verse16 And when we came to Rome, the centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard; but Paul was suffered to dwell by himself with a soldier that kept him. VerseEnd

Verse17 And it came to pass that after three days, Paul called the chief of the Jews together. And when they had come together, he said unto them, Men and brethren, though I have committed nothing against the people or customs of our fathers, yet was I delivered prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans, VerseEnd Verse18 who, when they had examined me, would have let me go because there was no cause of death in me. VerseEnd Verse19 But when the Jews spoke against it, I was constrained to appeal unto Caesar — not that I had anything to accuse my nation of. VerseEnd Verse20 For this cause therefore have I called for you: to see you and to speak with you, because for the hope of Israel I am bound with this chain. VerseEnd Verse21 And they said unto him, We neither received letters out of Judea concerning you, neither any of the brethren that came showed or spoke any harm of you. VerseEnd Verse22 But we desire to hear of you what you think; for as concerning this sect, we know that everywhere it is spoken against. VerseEnd

Verse23 And when they had appointed him a day, there came many to him, into his lodging, to whom he expounded and testified the kingdom of God, persuading them concerning Jesus, both out of the law of Moses and out of the prophets, from morning until evening. VerseEnd Verse24 And some believed the things which were spoken, and some believed not. VerseEnd Verse25 And when they agreed not among themselves, they departed, after Paul had spoken one word: Well spoke the holy ghost by Isaiah the prophet unto our fathers, VerseEnd Verse26 saying, Go unto this people and say, Hearing you shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing you shall see, and not perceive; VerseEnd Verse27 for the heart of this people is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes have they closed, lest they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them. VerseEnd Verse28 Be it known therefore unto you that the salvation of God is sent unto the Gentiles, and that they will hear it. VerseEnd Verse29 And when he had said these words, the Jews departed and had great reasoning among themselves. VerseEnd

Verse30 And Paul dwelled two whole years in his own hired house and received all that came in unto him, VerseEnd Verse31 preaching the kingdom of God and teaching those things which concern the Lord Jesus Christ with all confidence, no man forbidding him. VerseEnd
